1) Must-have design variables (structure)

Use these to build repeated-measures / mixed models:

ID (subject identifier)

Zeit / Zeitpunkt (timepoint; pick one and standardize)

Gruppe (piano vs active control)

Platte (plate / array batch)

Koordinate (often an array position / chip coordinate; batch-ish)

TraceFileName (useful for QC / linking raw data)

reihenfolge (measurement/order effects if relevant)

VP_plus_zeitpunkt / ID_Pl4_Zeit (handy unique row keys, but don’t use instead of ID+time)

Why: epigenetics is super sensitive to batch + repeated measures.

2) The epigenetic outcomes (your “m…” and “p…” columns)

These look like CpG sites (or methylation probes) around a locus:

m337 … m1 and p3, p7, p11, p19, p23, p25, p27

Model these as:

either DV = methylation (one probe at a time, or PCA/mean score),

or create a region score (e.g., mean/PC1 over a biologically defined set).

Tip: don’t keep them as-is if you have dozens—use either multiple-testing correction (probe-wise) or dimensionality reduction.

3) Music intervention exposure (dose)

This is often more predictive than just Group:

HomeworkD_0 / HomeworkW_0 … HomeworkD_1/W_1 … HomeworkD_2/W_2

HomeworkD3 / HomeworkW3 / HomeworkD9 / HomeworkW9

mean_homework_D / median_homework_D

Presence_sum / Presence / Presence_3 (attendance)

weeks_without_lessons_1 / weeks_without_lessons_2

weeks_with_online_lessons_1 / weeks_with_online_lessons_2

corona_1 / corona_2 (important disruption indicator)

These are gold for modelling training intensity → epigenetic change.

4) Music skill outcomes (what changed)

You have both self/EA ratings and teacher ratings at multiple timepoints:

Piano performance ratings

Piano_Technik_…, Piano_Rhythmus_…, Piano_Expressivität_…

Piano_Texttreue… (note reading / fidelity)

Piano_Zusammenspiel… (interplay)

Piano_Einsatz… (engagement/entry)

Piano_Fortschritt… (progress)

Aggregates: Technique_1/2, Rhythm_1/2, Expressivity_1/2, Notereading_1/2, Interplay_1/2, Engagement_1/2, Progress_1/2

Plus combined: PP_Technique, PP_Rhythm, PP_Expressivity, PP_Notereading, PP_Interplay, all_Engagement, all_Progress

Learning climate / experience (teacher + EA)

MEUV_*_EA_3Mon/6Mon/12Mon

MEUV_*_Teacher_3Mon/6Mon/9Mon/12Mon

Aggregates: Climate_1/2, Participation_1/2, Interaction_1/2, Joy_1/2

Combined: MC_Climate, MC_Participation, MC_Interaction, MC_Joy, MC_Engagement, MC_Progress

These can be:

outcomes (does methylation change track skill gains?)

mediators (Group → motivation/engagement → methylation)

5) Core epigenetic covariates (confounding control)

Even if your story is “music affects methylation”, you should control for:

Age_start

Sex

Platte (+ possibly Koordinate)

Smoking/alcohol/drugs (big methylation drivers):

rauchen (and B14* variables)

B15 alcohol*

B17 drugs*

BMI-ish:

B09a_groesse, B09b_gewicht

Sleep:

B03a_sleep_quality, B03b_sleep_duration, B03c_sleep_to_recover

Education / SES-ish:

C06_bildungsgrad, maybe cr_education, cr_work, cr_leisure_time, cr_total

If you have cell-type proportions (I don’t see obvious ones), those are usually top priority too.

6) “Nice to have” outcomes depending on your theory

Cognitive, motor, auditory, MRI-derived metrics show up later in your list:

gonogo_Err_, gonogo_RT_ (inhibition)

DSP_*, DSY, DSY_errors (memory/processing)

BAT_ , MDT_ , MSAPRO** (musical aptitude / perception-type measures)

SRT / L_SRT / R_SRT / L_Dev / R_Dev (hearing?)

MRI-ish volumes: TIV, LHIP/RHIP, Lput/Rput, LcbrMot/RcbrMot

These are useful if your paper is “music → brain/cognition → methylation” or you want richer phenotypes.

A good starting modelling plan (simple + defensible)
A) Intervention effect on methylation (primary)

Mixed model per CpG (or region score):

methylation ~ Gruppe * Zeitpunkt + Age_start + Sex + Platte (+ Koordinate) + smoking + (1|ID)

B) Dose–response

methylation change ~ mean_homework_D + Presence_sum + confounders + (1|ID)

C) Linking methylation to learning

methylation change ~ PP_Progress (or teacher progress) + confounders + (1|ID)

If you paste str(tau[, c("ID","Zeitpunkt","Gruppe","Platte","Sex","Age_start")]) (just that small subset), I can tell you exactly:

which variable is safest for timepoint,

whether Gruppe is coded cleanly,

and how to reshape it for longitudinal modelling in R (wide → long) without breaking IDs.
